blocks.text: PL/SQL adds variables and step-by-step instructions to Oracle SQL. A block can declare a value and use it in a statement.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.title: Run a small PL/SQL block

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE` writes a line to the client output buffer; the client must enable its display.

blocks.text: With DBMS Output enabled in the client, the block prints Books: 3.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Enable the client's DBMS Output display. The slash is a client command used by tools such as SQL*Plus, not part of the PL/SQL block itself.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change books to 5 and predict the line.
